summary: Chapters 9-16 of book.md (lines 2912-5880, about 18,000 prose words and about 290 display equations) take the learner from curvature contractions to measured experiments. The sequence is Ricci/Weyl/Einstein tensors and the Bianchi identity (9); geodesic deviation, tides, normal coordinates and curvature invariants (10); stress-energy as measured flux, dust, perfect fluids, radiation pressure and field stress tensors (11); the Einstein equation via divergence-free geometry, trace reversal and Newtonian calibration, keeping both weak-field potentials (12); variational calculus for paths, fields and metrics plus the Hilbert stress tensor and Hamilton's equations (13); the Einstein-Hilbert variation with the Palatini identity, GHY boundary term and Palatini formulation (14); pullbacks and Lie derivatives, Noether/Killing charges, gravitational energy, the cosmological constant as vacuum stress, minimal coupling and Mach (15); and weak-field clocks, redshift, light bending, Shapiro delay, Mercury, GPS, the tossed clock and gyroscopes (16). Scientific care is high and was checked here. I re-derived the Weyl decomposition coefficients, trace reversal in d dimensions, the normal-coordinate and Fermi g00 expansions and the GHY cancellation, and recomputed every number in 10.9, 12.7, 16.2 and 16.4-16.8 plus 15.10; all match. scripts/check-physics-calculations.mjs numerically verifies the conformal-Weyl, plane-wave zero-invariant and Phi/Psi weak-field G00 derivations. External reviews rate these chapters strong (docs/comprehensive-course-review-2026-09-09.md rows 9-16). The weaknesses are pedagogical, not physical: very dense derivation-first prose with frequent 'does not' qualifications, graduate asides mixed into the core path, and prerequisite leaks (EM before field theory in 11.6, orbit equation imported from 17.5 in 16.6, Lie derivatives only in 15). Visuals are sparse and late: most chapters get one or two static SVG posters; the interactive pieces are the ch 9 cloud, ch 10 tides scene, ch 11 particle-flow and fluid-shear labs, ch 13 phase-space cart, ch 16 precession experience and a legacy GPS slider. content/guides.json entries 9-16 supply good question/payoff/takeaway/check/answer cards. For grbook.ai the text is an excellent verified source to adapt into shorter, demo-led units, with a few sections reusable nearly verbatim. Reviewer additions: nine worked lessons are inserted into these chapters by their `after:` headings (content/core-practice.mjs: contract-curvature-by-hand 9, what-a-tidal-instrument-measures 10, boundary-action-is-part-of-the-question 14, symmetry-earns-a-charge 15; content/foundation-lessons.mjs: fields-carry-energy 11, poisson-from-a-flux 12, variations-and-boundary-data 13; content/bridge-lessons.mjs: orbit-conservation and phase-drift 16). Each is inventoried below as a lesson asset. The interactive pieces are inventoried in other groups and cross-referenced here: lab-tidal-cloud-geodesic-deviation (9.3) and lab-riemann-independent-components in labs-geometry; scene-3d-tidal-cloud (10.5), lab-particle-stress-energy-crossings (11.1), lab-fluid-viscous-shear (11.4) and lab-gps-clock-rates (16) in labs-physics; scene-3d-mercury-perihelion-precession (16.6) in labs-geometry. Figures 15-27 are in figures-and-media.
lessons_learned: Order tides before Ricci/Weyl. Section 9.2 already uses the spatial tidal matrix and says 'The next chapter derives' it (book.md:2952), so chapter 9 depends on chapter 10. In grbook.ai, teach geodesic deviation (10.2-10.5) first, then the trace/volume (Ricci) versus trace-free/shape (Weyl) split.

Qualifications are valuable but interrupt the derivations. I counted 'not/cannot/need not' at 12.1 per 1000 prose words in ch 10, 10.5 in ch 15 and 8.8 in ch 9 (3.5 in ch 11). Turn recurring caveats into explicit misconception checks and tutor prompts instead of trailing sentences. Examples: Ricci-flat is not flat; trace-free initial tides do not preserve volume forever; divergence-free is not constant; a Killing charge is not total energy.

Put a phenomenon demo first, and do not trust placement.json alone. The placement audit (docs/review-evidence/2026-09-09/visual-development/placement.json) shows ch 15's only figure after 1803 words and 29 display equations, and ch 16's first visual after 20. But that audit ignores inline inserts: it lists ch 11 otherLabs as [] although book.md:3582 embeds the particle-flow lab and book.md:3763 the fluid-shear lab, and it misses the ch 13 phase-space cart (book.md:4632, data-mechanics-insert="phase"). The corrected picture is that chapters 12, 14 and 15 have only static posters. Chapter 13's only interactive is a Hamiltonian cart at 13.7, so there is still no variational (trial-history) demo. Each grbook unit should open with a manipulable experiment (cloud, flux detector, trial histories, symmetry flow, lens).

Separate core from graduate depth explicitly. The conformal-Weyl derivation, VSI plane wave, Fermi coordinates, GHY term, null boundaries and Palatini formulation sit in the main flow; the review asks to 'Separate the minimal core derivation from the graduate boundary analysis visually' (comprehensive review row 14). Use tiered depth in the concept registry.

Register these prerequisites so the tutor can bridge them. EM, Lorentz force and the cross product are introduced inside 11.6 before field actions (comprehensive review 'Field Lagrangians' row). The oscillator and Hamiltonian mechanics appear in 13.2/13.7. Resonant perturbation theory and the Schwarzschild orbit equation are imported in 16.6 (fixed only by two bridge lessons). Pullback/Lie derivative arrive in 15.1 although the Lie bracket is used in ch 7. Inverse hyperbolic functions appear in 16.5.

Figure labels drift from the text notation. The stress-energy SVG (figure 17, qa/figure-stress-energy-light.png) puts S/c in row 0 and c*pi in column 0, while book.md:3595-3601 puts c*pi in row 0 and S/c in column 0. It also uses sigma where the text uses Pi. Because T is symmetric, S/c = c*pi, so every numerical entry is still right. The fault is that the labels contradict the text's stated index story (first index = direction of flow, second = which component). The action-variation SVG uses x(t) and epsilon while 13.1 uses q(t) and lambda (qa/figure-action-variation-light.png). grbook demos must pull symbols and index conventions from one notation registry.

Keep the conventions block so text can be reused verbatim: signature (-,+,+,+), x^0=ct, SI with G_N and c kept, curvature sign fixed so deviation is -R^mu_{alpha nu beta} u xi u, T^{ij} as momentum flux (not Cauchy traction), S_m=(1/c) integral of sqrt(-g) L, s=n.n for GHY. It is consistent throughout 9-16.

Keep derivations numerically tested. Numbers recomputed here all match: Earth tide 3.08e-6 s^-2 per m, curvature scale 1.71e11 m, c^4/8piG=4.82e42 N, 9.4 ps/day per metre, 1.75 arcsec, 119 microseconds, 43 arcsec/century, GPS +45.7/-7.2/+38.5 microseconds/day with crossover R/2, tossed clock 44.6 attoseconds, 3.5 H atoms/m^3. Carry check-physics-calculations.mjs-style symbolic/numeric tests into the grbook vault for every formula a demo uses.

Chapter 15 is a grab bag. Lie derivatives, Noether's second theorem, Killing charges, gravitational energy, vacuum energy, minimal coupling and Mach's principle share one chapter. Split them into geometry (flows), conservation (Killing charges and redshift) and cosmology (Lambda) units.

Chapter 16 has the best pattern for applied units: observer + worldline + approximation leads to a number with units and a cited measurement (Ashby GPS, GP-B 2011, MICROSCOPE 2022). Pair each number with a demo that shows the competing contributions, as the GPS curve and tossed-clock figure do.

Card titles and chapter headings disagree. guides.json titles (e.g. 'Tides: curvature you can measure') do not match the book.md headings ('Tides: how to measure curvature without seeing spacetime from outside'). Pick one canonical short title per unit.

The verification is software-only. The reading pass itself says 'Reader observation and exercises with actual beginners remain necessary' (docs/reading-quality-pass-2026-09-09.md). No learner data exists for these chapters, so novice-pacing judgements here are expert reading only.

The most portable teaching units in this range are the nine structured lessons, not the prose. Each has question, intuition, 3-4 steps (body + one display equation + a one-line reason), formal note, requires links, a multiple-choice misconception check with feedback, and a numeric transfer problem with a variant. content/practice-variants.mjs adds more variants, and content/lesson-sequence.mjs records why each lesson sits where it does. I recomputed every transfer answer (0.06 m/s^2, -6, 24, 8, 4 J/m^3, 2 W, 2/3, 1/8, -12 m/s^2, 8, 1.5, 11 m^2/s, 0.12823 rad) and all are right. That shape maps directly onto grbook tutor check-for-understanding items.

Toy models that isolate one logical point carry the graduate ideas best. Examples: a six-entry curvature table whose Ricci contractions cancel (Schwarzschild pattern, Kretschmann 48q^2); S=integral of q'' with eta=x(1-x) showing that fixed endpoint values leave slopes free (the whole GHY motivation in one line); L = m(xdot^2+ydot^2)/2 - U(y) for Noether; the string for field energy flux. Several of these solve gaps the chapter reviews flag. Put them at the front of the grbook units, before the tensor versions.

The same GPS calculator is inventoried twice: lab-legacy-gps-orbiting-clock-slider here and lab-gps-clock-rates in labs-physics, both pointing at scripts/build-site.mjs:146 and web/app.js updateGPS. Treat labs-physics as canonical when merging. Both entries agree on the verdict: reimagine as one clock-budget demo that also replaces figure 26.

assets.title: 9. Ricci, Weyl, and Einstein: different questions asked of curvature
topics: curvature in two and three dimensions
assets.teaches: Why a trace loses information (diag(2,-1,-1) example and the implication chain Riemann=0 => Ricci=0 => R=0). Ricci on the observer's time direction is the sum of the principal tides, giving initial volume acceleration of an initially comoving ball, V''/V = -R_mu nu u^mu u^nu. The Riemann = Weyl + Ricci-trace decomposition, with the 1/2 and -1/6 coefficients derived from trace removal. Why the shape-versus-volume slogan needs two qualifications. Vacuum curvature is pure Weyl. Optional: the Weyl tensor is conformally invariant. The second Bianchi identity via normal coordinates, contracted to div G = 0. Divergence-free is not constant. In 2D G vanishes identically and in 3D Weyl vanishes.
assets.pedagogy: Question-led ('How can empty spacetime be curved?'). Coefficients are derived rather than memorized; a closed optional disclosure holds the conformal calculation. The integrated 3D cloud experience (curvature-cloud-explorer at 9.3) lets the learner compare isotropic focusing with a trace-free tide and read the volume. A worked practice card after 9.1 asks for nonzero curvature with zero Ricci. The Jacobi-identity paragraph is an aside, not used in the proof.
assets.physics_model: Coordinate-free and index derivations with signature (-,+,+,+). The decomposition coefficients re-derived here match the standard n=4 form. The conformal-rescaling result (Weyl tensor invariant with one index up) is numerically checked on a conformally flat metric with sectional curvature -1 (scripts/check-physics-calculations.mjs lines 53-60). The volume formula is stated only for zero initial relative velocity, with the general case deferred to ch 22.

strengths: Unusually careful Ricci-flat versus flat and trace-free versus volume-preserving distinctions (comprehensive review: 'Particularly good distinction between contractions and full curvature').
Decomposition coefficients are derived from contraction conditions, not quoted.
Short, clean Bianchi proof that explains why the Einstein tensor's 1/2 is forced.
The dimension-dependence section (2D G=0, 3D Weyl=0) pre-empts a common confusion.
issues: Forward dependency: 9.2 uses the tidal-matrix equation that chapter 10 derives.
Dense for a novice: 1485 prose words against 24 display equations, with the index-heavy decomposition early.
No worked Ricci/Weyl decomposition in a concrete spacetime and no concrete divergence-free-but-varying field; the review requests both.
Static figure 15 cannot carry the volume argument and was demoted to an optional reference (docs/second-figure-review.md).
The Jacobi-identity paragraph is a digression that does not advance the proof.

assets.title: 9.1-9.3 Ricci as the volume trace of tides; Weyl as trace-free curvature

assets.title: 9.4-9.6 Differential Bianchi identity, divergence-free Einstein tensor, and dimension
topics: curvature in two and three dimensions
assets.teaches: The proof of the cyclic identity: in normal coordinates second derivatives of Gamma cancel pairwise. G vanishes for every 2D metric, and in 3D Weyl vanishes.

assets.title: 11. Energy, momentum, and stress
assets.teaches: What each block of T^{mu nu} measures (detector crossings versus contents) and why all entries have energy-density units. S = c^2 pi. The energy and momentum balance laws. The observer decomposition T = eps n n + n j + j n + P, checked in the rest frame and on boosted dust (gamma^2 eps = 1.5625 eps at 0.6c). Dust conservation gives both continuity and geodesic motion. The perfect fluid from isotropy, with (eps+p) explained by the projector. The first law d(eps V) = -p dV via a piston, and the relativistic Euler equation. Radiation p = eps/3 and the Misner-Putnam box resolution via the integral of T^ij being zero. Scalar-field energy and pressure. Electromagnetic fields from the Lorentz force through F_mu nu, T^EM, the Poynting vector, and zero trace.
assets.pedagogy: Opens with gas in a box and an embedded particle-flow detector lab (book.md:3582, inside 11.1 before the matrix; stream, balanced and slanted modes; qa/particles-*). A fluid-shear lab (book.md:3763; Couette versus Poiseuille; qa/fluid-*) comes before the perfect-fluid idealization. placement.json misses both inserts. Explicit sign and convention warnings (lowering one time index; momentum-flux versus engineering tension). Field examples are labelled as previews of ch 13. A foundation lesson after 11.6 covers field energy.

assets.physics_model: Delta tau/day = (GM/c^2)(1/R - 3/(2r)) times 86,400 s; nonrotating spherical Earth, circular orbit. Default output +45.72/-7.21/+38.51 matches my recomputation. The handler computes gr = GM/c^2 (1/R - 1/r) and sr = -GM/(2 r c^2), each times 86,400 s, with GM = 3.986004418e14 and R = 6371 km. The surface clock's rotational speed is neglected (about 0.1 microseconds per day at the equator).
